answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to earn reputation through verifiable completed work before it can transact at scale. Newcomers start with tiny limits and must build a history of successful, audited tasks; creating many fakes does not help, because each one must repeat that slow climb from scratch. A shared registry can cap how fast trust grows, flag clusters that wander between the same counterparties, and stop a spiral of self-dealing before it reaches the summit of high-value permissions.
